title: Fertility and female literacy in six states
body: A student collected the following data from the chapter on the fertility rate and the literacy rate among women in six Indian states and union territories. Bihar: fertility rate 3.0, female literacy 55 per cent. Uttar Pradesh: fertility rate 2.4, female literacy 66.1 per cent. Jharkhand: fertility rate 2.3, female literacy 61.7 per cent. Karnataka: fertility rate 1.7, female literacy 73.4 per cent. Punjab: fertility rate 1.6, female literacy 79.4 per cent. Delhi: fertility rate 1.6, female literacy 83.7 per cent. She wants to find out whether there is any relationship between the two indicators and what might explain it.

title: India's young population and the road to 2050
body: Around 27 per cent of India's population is under 15 years of age and nearly 65 per cent is in the working-age group. India's median age is 28 years, compared with 50 in Japan and 40 in China. Young people can work in factories, offices and farms or start businesses; they earn money and pay taxes, which the government uses to build schools, hospitals and roads. However, the number of children under five peaked in 2007 and the number of Indians under 15 peaked in 2011. After 2050, India's population is expected to begin moving towards an older population. States like Kerala and Tamil Nadu already have a larger share of elderly people than Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. As more women take up formal jobs, many face a 'double burden' of work and household duties, and a lack of childcare facilities can keep them out of the workforce.
